records.reason: Class U−: "But as for these enemies of mine, who did not want me to reign over them, bring them here and slaughter them before me." Tertullian's point in 4.37.4 is that the parable shows God as a judge "even on the side of severity", and he finds that severity in the master taking away what the servant seemed to have (19:26). The command to slaughter the master's enemies would have been his strongest evidence, and he does not cite it. Restored by method (METHOD §11): by its mechanics, the parable sets two groups going at the departure: the servants given money (19:13) and the citizens who refuse his reign (19:14). He returns "having received the kingdom" (19:15) and reckons with the servants (19:15–26); the citizens are reckoned with only here. Read inwardly, the enemies who refuse his reign are what in the person refuses it, and their death "before him" is that refusal ended in his presence: the enemy's power trodden (10:19), the enemies a footstool (20:43). In the final text the parable frames the going up and the king hailed (19:28, 19:38). Reading: docs/research/correspondence/word_by_word.md, chapter 17, test of 19:27; second_pass.md §2.

records.reason: Class U?: "After he had said this, he went on ahead, going up to Jerusalem." A one-verse NA27 paragraph with no attested verse; it introduces the entry (19:29–46). Restored by method (METHOD §11): by its mechanics, the road set at 9:51 ("he set his face to go to Jerusalem") is named again at 17:11 and 19:11 ("because he was near Jerusalem"), and without 19:28–46 it never arrives: from "near Jerusalem" the text goes to "in the temple" (20:1), with no going up, no descent of the mountain with "peace in heaven, and glory in the highest", no weeping over the city whose peace is hidden from its eyes, and no entering the house of prayer. By its words, 20:2 "by what authority do you do these things?" has its first object in 19:45–46. Reading: docs/research/correspondence/word_by_word.md, chapter 17, tests of 19:28 and 19:29–46.

By its words, 20:2 "by what authority do you do these things?" has its first object in 19:45–46. Reading: docs/research/correspondence/word_by_word.md, chapter 17, tests of 19:28 and 19:29–46. Printed against Marcion's text: the witnesses state that the passage was not in it.
